semantic_rows.reasoning: Direct investment-banking execution across M&A, restructurings and capital markets with hands-on modelling and valuation; a second-pass challenge on placement seniority does not outweigh the genuinely target deal content.

Core front-office equity execution, client order flow and market-microstructure work align directly with markets execution; the sales component is meaningful but does not disprove the execution-led fit.

End-to-end corporate M&A work spanning strategic assessment, valuation, due diligence and transaction execution is a direct target fit; the manager title does not disprove Strong because the role remains hands-on in live deals.

Real-estate capital-markets advisory with valuation, due diligence, negotiation and end-to-end transaction leadership is direct deal execution; the sector specialization narrows scope but does not weaken the core transaction fit.

Substantive financial-risk modelling and portfolio analysis are relevant, but the role is deliberately mixed with non-financial risk, regulatory implementation, governance and credit-model work rather than consistently market/liquidity-risk execution.

The day-to-day work is trade reconciliation, static-data maintenance, settlement-break resolution and investment-system support, making it investment-adjacent operations rather than investment decision-making or markets execution.

Buy-side and sell-side M&A execution, valuation modelling and transaction support from kick-off to closing are directly on target; the research and presentation tasks are supporting components rather than evidence against Strong.
